knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A wet area near the meter with pressure drop across zones suggests a supply-side leak. The technician isolates the zone if allowed, does not work on the meter, and refers the fault.
The approved service-locating check comes before excavation. Unexpected services are reported and digging stops until their location and status are confirmed.
Isolating the zone valve stops the water quickly. The technician then decides whether the repair is zone-side and in scope, or referred.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied mock zone system with a simulated leak, the learner locates the leak on the zone map and isolates the zone valve within the assessor's set time, confirming the water has stopped.
Given a supplied scenario card describing a supply-side leak, the learner writes a referral that states the location, symptoms and the next step, without attempting the repair.
The learner states the service-locating step they would follow before a supplied mock excavation and stops the simulated excavation at the assessor's unexpected-service card.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Leak location and isolation record for the mock system, signed by the assessor.
Referral note for the supplied supply-side scenario.
Assessor observation record of the service-locating step.
stopWorkCriteria: Working on the mock meter, backflow device or supply connection during the assessment.
Excavating after an unexpected service card has been presented.
Leaving a simulated zone running after the leak has been identified.
